extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who are members of or seeking membership in the District of Columbia Bar; Bar administrators and Board of Governors
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing membership, registration, classes, fees, reinstatement, officer roles, governance (Board/Executive Committee), meetings, referenda, disbursements, bylaws, and amendments for the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after failure to pay assessed late fee/returned payment fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who has been administratively suspended for failure to pay the required assessed late fee and/or returned payment fee shall be reinstated upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) payment of the required assessed late fee and/or returned payment fee by April 30th of the annual license year in which the suspension occurred; and (c) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if such member was admitted after July 1, 1994, and has not yet completed the course, or such member was admitted before July 1, 1994, but has been suspended for five years or more and has not yet completed the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request for reinstatement is received after April 30th of the annual license year in which the suspension occurred, the member shall be reinstated in accordance with procedures listed in Section E.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of new admittees suspended for failing Mandatory Course
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly admitted attorneys of the Bar suspended for failure to complete the Mandatory Course shall be reinstated upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course; (c) payment of any required outstanding license fee; (d) payment of a reinstatement fee; and (e) submission of a statement that the member is not suspended, temporarily suspended, or disbarred by any disciplinary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of retired or resigned members
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who has elected the Retired class of membership or who has been approved to voluntarily resign may request change in membership class or reinstatement to Active, Inactive, or Judicial membership upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) payment of the annual license fee for the current annual license year; (c) payment of a reinstatement fee; and (d) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if such member was admitted after July 1, 1994 and has not yet completed the course, or such member has not been in the Active class of membership for five years or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The purposes of the Bar shall be (a) to assist the legal profession in maintaining high standards of the practice of law in the District of Columbia; (b) to aid the courts of the District of Columbia Court in carrying out and improving the administration of justice; (c) to promote access to justice and enhance the delivery of legal services to those in need; (d) to foster and maintain high ideals of integrity, learning, competence in public service, and high ethical standards of conduct; (e) to safeguard the proper professional interests of the members of the Bar; (f) to encourage the formation and support the activities of volunteer bar associations; (g) to provide a forum for and publish information about discussion of subjects pertaining to the practice of law, jurisprudence and law reform, and the relationship of the Bar to the public; and (h) to carry on a continuing program of legal research and education in substantive law, practice and procedure, and make reports and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the official objectives guiding Bar activities, publications, education, and policy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is included in membership
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons admitted to practice law in the District of Columbia are organized as the District of Columbia Bar. Residence in the District of Columbia shall not be a condition of eligibility to membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every attorney who engages in the practice of law within the District of Columbia (as defined in Rule 49(b), exclusive of those described in Rule 49(c)) shall on or before July 1 of every year file with the Secretary of the Bar a registration statement setting forth current residence and office addresses, email address, telephone number, other state jurisdictions of admission including date of admission, and such other information as the Court may direct. Supplemental statement must be filed within thirty days of any change. An attorney newly subject shall file within three months or by the following July 1, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request, acknowledgement of receipt shall be provided by the Secretary. Failure to file after due notice may result in summary suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to file registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney who fails to file any registration statement or supplement in accordance with the requirements shall, after due notice from the Secretary of the Bar, be summarily suspended from membership by the Board of Governors and thereby shall be barred from practicing law in the District of Columbia until reinstated as provided under § 8 of this Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for attorneys assuming inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney who has retired or is not engaged in practice shall advise the Secretary of the Bar in writing or through electronic means that he or she desires to assume inactive status and discontinue the practice of law. Upon filing such notice, that attorney shall no longer be eligible to practice law but shall continue to file registration statements for 5 years thereafter so they may be located if any complaint is made about past conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon the filing of notice to assume inactive status, the attorney shall be removed from the roll of active members unless and until granted reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Course for new admittees (establishment and requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Bar shall establish and administer a course on the District of Columbia Rules of Professional Conduct and on District of Columbia practice to be presented at least six times per year. Within twelve months after admission, all members admitted after July 1, 1994 shall complete the course and certify compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar must report annually to the Court on the course addressing curriculum, faculty, number of presentations, attendance, and number suspended for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and suspension for failing to complete Mandatory Course
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney admitted after July 1, 1994, who fails to complete the course within twelve months after admission shall receive written notice of noncompliance. Any attorney who fails to comply within sixty days after issuance of such notice shall be suspended from membership in the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after suspension for failure to complete Mandatory Course
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member otherwise in good standing who is suspended for failure to complete the Mandatory Course shall be reinstated upon completion of the course and fulfillment of such other administrative requirements as the Board of Governors may impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of membership and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Members shall be divided into classes such as 'active', 'judicial', 'inactive', and 'retired'. The inactive class is limited to persons eligible for active membership but not engaged in practice in D.C. Judges of courts of record and certain judicial officers shall be classified as judicial members. Retired members must have been an active member for five years (with limited substitutions) and have been engaged in practice for a total of 25 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No judicial, inactive, or retired member shall be entitled to practice law in D.C. or to hold office or vote in general elections of the Bar, except as provided in Rule 49(c). The Board may create additional membership classes after consultation with the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of license fees/membership dues (ceiling and determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every member shall pay dues in an amount not to exceed a ceiling set by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals. The Board of Governors shall determine the amount of license fees/dues to be paid annually by members in the various classes of membership. All dues shall be paid to the Treasurer and constitute a fund for payment of Bar expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may make recommendations to the Court concerning the ceiling; if so published, members have 60 days to comment. Recommendations to increase the dues ceiling shall not be subject to referendum under Rule VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-payment consequences and late charges
rubrics_metrics.description: If the annual dues of any member remain unpaid at the expiration of 90 days from when due, the membership may be suspended by the Board of Governors in the manner provided in the Bylaws. The Board may impose a reasonable late charge to offset notification costs. If the late charge is not timely paid, membership may be suspended. No person suspended for nonpayment shall be entitled to practice law during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary resignation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A member in good standing and not under investigation may file with the Secretary of the Bar and with Disciplinary Counsel written or electronic notice of election to discontinue the practice of law in D.C. and to terminate membership. Upon written notice of acceptance of such resignation from the Secretary after consultation with Disciplinary Counsel, the person shall cease to be a member and be removed from the membership register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and reinstatement governance
rubrics_metrics.description: A member’s resignation from and reinstatement into the Bar shall be governed by procedures prescribed by the Bar, which shall include consultation with the Office of Disciplinary Counsel. Reinstatement following suspension, assumption of inactive status, or resignation shall be governed by rules promulgated by the Board of Governors after consultation with the Board on Professional Responsibility of the Court. The Board may reinstate an attorney nunc pro tunc in an appropriate case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to the Clerk of status changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Bar shall forward forthwith to the Clerk of the Court the names of those attorneys who have filed registration statements and those whose membership status has been changed in any way pursuant to this Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer eligibility, term, and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers shall be a President, a President‑elect, a Secretary, and a Treasurer, who shall be nominated and elected or appointed as provided in the Bylaws. Only active members shall be eligible to serve as officers. The term of office of each officer shall be one year and until the election and qualification of a successor. The officers shall receive no compensation for their services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties of officers and process for filling vacancies are set forth in the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of specific officers
rubrics_metrics.description: President: preside at meetings of the Bar and Board of Governors, appoint committees, be ex officio member of all committees. President‑elect: perform duties during President's absence and succeed to President at term end. Secretary: act as secretary at meetings, keep records, notify officers/committee members, prepare and maintain member register, send notices. Treasurer: receive, collect, and keep funds, disburse under Board direction, render reports, assist in preparing annual budget, furnish surety bond as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacancies and succession for President and President‑elect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the President dies, is permanently disabled, or resigns, the President‑elect may succeed to the office for the remainder of the term and subsequently the presidential term for which elected. If the President‑elect declines, the Board shall elect one of its members to serve as President for remainder of term; that person shall resign from the Board and the vacancy filled per rules. If vacancy occurs in President‑elect on or after January 1 by death, disability, or resignation, the Board shall elect one of its members to assume duties as Vice President (not succeed to President). If vacancy occurs prior to January 1, a special election shall be held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Secretary/Treasurer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any duties imposed on the Secretary or Treasurer may be performed under their supervision by assistants or employees of the Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Board of Governors
rubrics_metrics.description: The affairs of the Bar shall be managed by a Board of Governors consisting of the officers of the Bar and the immediate past‑president as ex officio members, and fifteen members elected by the members of the Bar as prescribed by the Bylaws. The Treasurer‑elect shall be among the fifteen elected, non‑officer members and serve as an at‑large member after completing their year as Treasurer. The Board may appoint non‑voting members as prescribed by the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board term limits and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial elected Board members' terms were staggered (1, 2, 3 years). Thereafter, newly elected members serve 3‑year terms. Board members continue to serve until successors are elected and qualified. No person shall be eligible to serve on the Board unless an active member, and no person shall be eligible for election to the Board for more than two consecutive 3‑year terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Governors functions and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall have general charge of the affairs and activities of the Bar, including authority to fix time/place of annual meeting; make appropriations and authorize disbursements; engage and define duties/compensation of employees; receive, consider and act on committee reports; arrange publication of official bulletin; conduct investigations of matters affecting the Bar; fill vacancies in Board or offices; and adopt Bylaws and regulations not inconsistent with these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition and quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an Executive Committee consisting of the President, the President‑elect, the immediate past president and four additional members selected annually by the Board of Governors from among their number. Five members shall constitute a quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee powers and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee may exercise all powers and perform duties of the Board between Board meetings, except it shall not, unless otherwise authorized by the Board: (a) amend the Bylaws, (b) make rules for regulations governing nominations or elections, or (c) initiate the taking of any referendum or poll of members of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee shall perform duties prescribed by the Board; minutes must be kept and distributed to Board members immediately after each meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public expressions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion of the Bar on any matter involving legislation of major public interest or concern or of major importance to the members of the Bar shall be publicly expressed unless authorized by the Board of Governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual and special meetings (timing and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an annual meeting of members during June each year. The Board shall determine time/place and arrange a suitable program. Notice of the time/place of every annual meeting shall be mailed to each active member or published in the official bulletin at least 30 days prior. Notice of special meetings shall be mailed or published at least 10 days prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special meeting by petition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Special meetings shall be called by the Secretary whenever he or she receives a petition signed by not less than 3% of the active members requesting such meeting and specifying the purpose; the meeting shall be convened not later than 30 days after Secretary receives petition. The Bar census is determined as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and virtual attendance at meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred active members present at any annual or special meeting shall constitute a quorum. No member shall be entitled to be represented by proxy. 'Present' includes in‑person attendance, virtual/electronic attendance, or a combination so long as all attendees can hear each other and participate meaningfully during such meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations from the assembly to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The members present at any annual or special meeting may consider and by vote adopt proposals pertinent to the purposes of the Bar; every such adopted proposal shall constitute a recommendation from the assembly to the Board of Governors and shall be referred accordingly, except where the proposal is a direction for a referendum under Rule VII or a proposal for amendment of these rules under Rule XIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may at any time, by the affirmative vote of 2/3 of its membership, refer to the active members of the Bar by mail ballot any question of Bar policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by assembly resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit for determination by the active members any question of Bar policy including proposed changes in the rules or Bylaws whenever directed by resolution adopted at any annual or special meeting by the affirmative vote of not less than 200 active members, provided such resolution is adopted at two consecutive meetings of the assembly to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by member petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit for determination by member ballots any question of Bar policy, including proposals for changes in the Rules or Bylaws, whenever directed by a petition signed by not less than 3% of the active members of the Bar based on the census as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballots for any referendum shall be prepared, distributed, returned and counted in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors. The result of a referendum, as determined by a majority of the votes cast, when duly ascertained shall be published by the Board and shall control the action of the Bar, Board, officers and committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursements, accounting, and audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall make necessary appropriations for disbursements from funds to pay all necessary expenses. It shall cause proper books of account to be kept and procure an annual audit by a certified public accountant. At each annual meeting the Board shall present a financial statement showing assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements. A copy shall be filed with the Clerk of the Court and published in an official Bar publication prior to the annual meeting. The copy filed with the Clerk shall be accompanied by a detailed statement reflecting all significant components of the Bar's total disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation and amendment of Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws not inconsistent with these Rules may be established by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two‑thirds of the voting Board members in attendance. Proposals for amendment of the Rules may be presented to the Court by petition of the Board or by petition of the assembly in respect of changes approved by referendum; hearings will be pursuant to notice as the Court may direct. Bylaws may be amended or abrogated by majority vote of the voting members of the Board at a meeting with at least two‑thirds of the voting members present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of the Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Bar Rules shall take effect on April 1, 1972, on which date the association shall be deemed to have come into existence.
